key_insight: UNSM changed the local hardness of Cr3C2–NiCr coatings in a strongly sample-dependent way, with DS coatings reaching 820–970 HV and HVOF coatings spanning a wider 546–1165 HV range.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests surface modification can improve or redistribute near-surface mechanical response in thermal-sprayed wear coatings, but process condition and coating route must be optimized individually.
method: Detonation-sprayed (DS) and HVOF Cr3C2–NiCr coatings were treated by ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification.
Four treated samples per deposition route were tested using two static loads (20 and 30 N) and two vibration amplitudes (20 and 30 µm).
Instrumental hardness was measured at 300 mN / 10 s, and post-scratch morphology was examined by SEM.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardness values and SEM post-scratch observations for the treated samples, with the highest hardness seen in DS-T1 at 20 N/20 µm and HVOF-T4 at 30 N/30 µm.
watch_item: The SEM findings are qualitative and do not isolate UNSM-induced damage or establish a definitive scratch-resistance ranking.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
